text:
Frank Nazar has nine goals in his last ten games, and the Blackhawks have rewarded him with more ice time, 1:44 more a night over that stretch. At 22 he's now at 12 goals and 16 points in 23 games, eight of them on the power play, and he plays with real speed: his top skating speed sits in the 90th percentile.

How much of it is real? Some. His chances are up a little, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 62% of his entries last season. But he's shooting 24%, against 11% a year ago, on 8.28 expected goals (a measure of chance quality). That finishing rate rarely lasts. The Athletic's Scott Powers counted the Moore-Nazar-Kane line 19th in expected goals among lines with 75 minutes together, so the shifts themselves have been good. Our numbers project 30 goals, which builds in some cooling. The bigger minutes are the part worth watching.
headline: Frank Nazar's hot streak: real chances, hotter finishing
